column1: # S1b follow-up: a finer partial grid (2026-10-23; the user). POST HOC and labelled
# as such: the pre-registered rung-4 verdicts (F12c: S1b against) stand as reported.
# r1c-none (arms/rung1_cara.tsv) with BANKRUN_PARTIAL_STEPS=20, i.e. fractions in
# steps of 0.05 instead of {0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1}. Same seed offset and common
# seeding, so it pairs with r1c-none run for run.
# Question: is S1b's failure an artefact of the grid? In r1c-none the largest agent
# never split: in all 223 of its exits every interior fraction drained the bank, so
# the drain rule left only 0 or 1. A finer grid offers fractions just short of
# draining it. Reading, stated before the run:
#   - the largest agent takes interior fractions in some exits, S1b < 0
#       -> the failure was the grid's; the finer grid is the reference for the sweep;
#   - it still exits all at once (one-shot share ~1.0)
#       -> structural: at N = 1,000 the largest depositor is the last straw; only
#          super-individuals (or a smaller largest share) address it.
# Also read: the S1 curve by size group against r1c-none and Celsius, and P(fail)
# paired with r1c-none (a finer grid changes the bank's path, not only the label).
# Reader: python3 scripts/rung4_stats.py --arm outputs/r4-g20 --ref outputs/r1c-none
# Cost: only decisions above PARTIAL_MIN_SHARE re-simulate per fraction (19 vs 3).
